findings.title: Fallback locales are only preloaded in the controller before_filter
findings.body: Translations are loaded on demand. `translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`, so the fallback locales (site default and :en) are loaded only by this `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that does not go through this filter has no fallback data loaded. That includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers, `I18n.with_locale` blocks and rake tasks. If a key is missing in the user's locale, the fallback chain [locale, default, :en] finds nothing because :en may not be loaded in that process. The result is a 'translation missing: ...' string, not the English text. A fresh worker process hits this on its first email in a non-English locale. The loading belongs in the accelerator, for example `translate`/`load_locale` loading the whole fallback chain, not in one controller filter.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain and caches missing-translation results
findings.body: The cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With this PR the result also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the custom fallback chain) and on which fallback locales are already loaded. Two consequences follow. (1) If an admin changes the default locale, entries cached for other locales still hold text from the old fallback until they are evicted or the process restarts. (2) If a lookup runs before the fallback locales are loaded, the frozen 'translation missing' string is stored under that key. It is then served on every later call, even after :en has been loaded. The key should include the fallback chain, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale changes. Missing-translation results should not be cached.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, and a hook in `set_locale`. It also removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from the production configs, which makes fallbacks active in every environment, including test and development. No spec covers any of this. Missing coverage includes: a key missing in the user locale falling back to the site default and then English, ordering and de-duplication of the chain, loading of fallback locales on demand, and interaction with the translation cache. Regressions in this globally applied behavior would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Every fallback lookup reads SiteSetting and allocates a new array
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is called by the I18n Fallbacks backend on every `translate_no_cache` call. Each call evaluates `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` and builds and de-duplicates a new array. This sits on the hot translation path that the accelerator exists to speed up. Because `[]` is overridden to always compute, nothing is memoized. It also makes translation depend on `SiteSetting` being available, which can fail early in boot or in rake tasks before the DB is ready. A `locale` passed as a String is not de-duplicated against the Symbols in the list.
